title: Well and Smile
premise: Rafael Okafor's late-night radio show becomes a séance when callers begin phoning in — people who died the week before, all asking him to 'count them out.' When every photograph from his grandmother's house starts showing an extra empty chair, Rafael realizes the house itself is keeping a tally, and each new chair means someone in the family will be taken. With his estranged sister Amara and her daughter Nia, he returns to the decaying family home to break the count before it reaches them. The ending demands a terrible arithmetic: Rafael takes the final chair himself, trading his place among the living for his family's — but because he documented everything on air, his voice keeps broadcasting from somewhere, counting down to nothing at all.
about_author: Theo Reyes is the pen name of a former overnight radio producer who spent years answering calls from insomniacs, grief-stricken strangers, and the occasional voice that shouldn't have been there. They write horror about families who survive by telling the truth too late.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Rafael hosts his 2 a.m. call-in show when a listener describes her own funeral from last Tuesday. He assumes a prank until she names details no one could know. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: professional skepticism curdling into private dread.

chapters.title: The Second Caller
chapters.summary: A man who drowned in the reservoir calls asking Rafael to 'count me out.' Station manager Priya threatens to pull the show; Rafael secretly begins recording everything. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the compulsion to document as armor against disbelief.

chapters.title: Grandma's House, Annotated
chapters.summary: Sorting his late grandmother's belongings, Rafael notices an extra wooden chair in every old photograph — one that was never there. His niece Nia points it out first, innocently. POV: Rafael with Nia. Emotional beat: childhood nostalgia turning uncanny.

chapters.title: Amara Answers the Door
chapters.summary: Estranged sister Amara arrives after years of silence, drawn by a voicemail of static that whispered her name. She doesn't believe Rafael until she sees the chair in her wedding photo. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: resentment and fear braided together.

chapters.title: The Count Begins
chapters.summary: A new chair appears in a photo taken that morning. That night, Uncle Emile dies in his sleep across town. The family does the math and hates the answer. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into urgency.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Nia finds grandma's journal: the house counts kin, and chairs can be filled or emptied, but never ignored. The family drafts rules — stay together, speak names aloud, never sit alone. POV: Nia. Emotional beat: a child imposing order on terror.

chapters.title: Callers From the Well
chapters.summary: The dead callers reveal they are all relatives, held in something beneath the house — an old well grandma sealed decades ago. They beg Rafael to stop the count before it fills its last chair. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: guilt over bloodlines he never chose.

chapters.title: What Grandma Sealed
chapters.summary: Through the journal and a neighbor's memory, the family learns grandma bargained with the well in 1963 to save her dying husband — a debt deferred, now due with interest. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: inherited sin, inherited courage.

chapters.title: The Empty Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rafael broadcasts live from the house; listeners hear the dead singing underneath his voice. The station fires him, but the recording spreads online — other families recognize their own extra chairs. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: isolation becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Nia Draws the Chairs
chapters.summary: Nia sketches every chair from every photo and discovers the count isn't linear — it skips, doubles back, and always ends with whoever holds the oldest grievance. Everyone looks at Amara. POV: Nia. Emotional beat: the cruelty of patterns.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Together
chapters.summary: The family holds vigil in the parlor, telling truths they've buried — Amara's abandonment, Rafael's silence, grandma's bargain. The walls sweat cold. A chair scrapes closer. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: confession as fortification.

chapters.title: Cousin Denny
chapters.summary: Denny, the black-sheep cousin, arrives uninvited and sits in the extra chair to prove it's nonsense. By morning he's gone, and his photo shows him already seated among the dead. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: horror at how cheaply the count can be fed.

chapters.title: Down the Sealed Stair
chapters.summary: Behind the pantry, the family finds stairs descending to the well cap, warm to the touch. The dead callers' voices rise through the floorboards like water through cracks. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: dread of descent.

chapters.title: Priya Calls Back
chapters.summary: Former station manager Priya, now convinced, brings archive tapes proving this has happened to three generations of Okafor-adjacent families. Every family that broke the count lost someone anyway. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: hope complicated by precedent.

chapters.title: The Bargain Reversed
chapters.summary: The journal's final pages describe how to unmake the deal: someone must volunteer for the last chair willingly, renaming the debt so it passes out of the bloodline. No one says who. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: love expressed as silent competition.

chapters.title: Nia Is Counted
chapters.summary: A new photo shows Nia seated in the extra chair. Panic fractures the family's fragile unity; Amara nearly burns the house down around them. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: maternal terror at full burn.

chapters.title: The Renaming
chapters.summary: Rafael realizes the well responds to broadcast — to being witnessed. He plans a final show from the well room, where naming the dead aloud might rename the debt itself. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: resolve built from documentation-as-prayer.

chapters.title: Broadcast From Below
chapters.summary: At 2 a.m., Rafael goes live from beneath the house, reading every dead relative's name into the open air. The well answers through the microphone, offering terms. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: awe and bargaining.

chapters.title: The Last Chair
chapters.summary: The well will release Nia and end the count if a living Okafor sits willingly and stays. Rafael lies to Amara about which of them it must be. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: Count Me Out
chapters.summary: Rafael sits. The house exhales; chairs vanish from every photograph; Nia wakes whole. Amara finds his recorder still running, capturing a final message. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: victory indistinguishable from loss.

chapters.title: Static and Grace
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Amara and Nia rebuild their lives around the recordings. On air once more, Rafael's voice comes through the studio line, calm, counting down — not to a death, but to zero, to nothing owed. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: peace beyond the threshold.

chapters.title: Well and Smile
chapters.summary: Nia, older now, visits the sealed house and finds one photograph remaining: Rafael in the extra chair, smiling, surrounded by the family finally gathered complete. She leaves flowers and turns off the light. POV: Nia. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into inheritance.
